title: Seller Property Condition Disclosure (Caveat Emptor State)
description: Kentucky does not mandate a comprehensive seller disclosure form for residential transactions. Kentucky follows a caveat emptor (buyer beware) principle. However, sellers must not actively conceal known material defects and must answer buyer questions honestly. KRS §324.360 requires licensees to disclose material adverse facts actually known to the licensee.

required_actions.note: No state-mandated disclosure form. Best practice: use KREC-recommended disclosure form voluntarily. Seller cannot actively conceal known defects.

title: Agency Disclosure and Consent
description: Kentucky requires licensees to disclose their agency relationship in writing at the earliest practicable time. Dual agency is permitted only with informed written consent of all parties. KRS §324.360(3) mandates the disclosure.

title: Radon Disclosure
description: Kentucky law requires that sellers or their agents provide buyers with an EPA-approved radon pamphlet and disclose any known radon test results or radon mitigation systems. KRS §211.9109 establishes the radon program and disclosure obligations.

required_actions.note: Provide EPA 'A Citizen's Guide to Radon' pamphlet.

title: Closing Type — Attorney Not Required
description: Kentucky does not require an attorney to be present at closing. Closings are typically conducted by title companies or settlement agents. However, preparation of deeds and other legal documents may constitute the practice of law under KRS §524.130.

required_actions.note: Title company or attorney typically handles closing. Attorney not legally required but recommended for complex transactions.

title: Lead-Based Paint Disclosure (Pre-1978)
description: Federal law (42 USC §4852d) requires sellers and landlords of housing built before 1978 to disclose known lead-based paint hazards. Kentucky follows the federal requirement. Sellers must provide the EPA pamphlet 'Protect Your Family From Lead in Your Home' and allow 10-day inspection period.
